item.title: Your Agent's Shell Allowlist Is Bypassable
item.description: Every shipmates crew member runs shell commands, and before any of them runs it goes through a permission gate. The gate uses the same rule syntax as Claude Code settings, Bash(git status), Bash(rm *), Write(**/.claude/settings.json), merged from several layers: a fleet-wide deny list pushed from Fleet Command, per-persona policy files, project settings, and the Brig, which compiles shipmates’ fifteen “Ship’s Articles” into deny and ask rules. Deny beats ask, ask beats allow.

item.title: shipmates Short Ones: 8 Minutes Extracting Go, and Three Voice-Loop Bugs
item.description:
A few shipmates bugs that don’t need a whole post each but were too good to leave in commit messages.

setup-go spends 8 minutes extracting Go on Windows CI

shipmates CI runs on my own ephemerd runners, and on Windows those jobs run inside a Hyper-V utility VM. The windows-x64 leg kept timing out in actions/setup-go. Here’s the log from PR #48:

20:58:46  Setup go version spec 1.26.6
20:58:46  Attempting to download 1.26.6...     <- tool-cache MISS
20:58:48  Acquiring 1.26.6 from ...zip
20:58:53  Extracting Go...
21:06:46  ERROR: The action 'Run actions/setup-go@v5' has timed out after 8 minutes

Seven seconds from the start of the step to Extracting Go..., then almost eight minutes extracting until the step timeout killed it.

item.title: shipmates: Persona-Based AI Coding Crews That Remember
item.description:
Since June most of my evenings have gone into shipmates, a Go CLI and daemon for running crews of AI coding agents. I tagged v0.5.0 on August 17th, two months and about 240 commits after the first architecture doc, so it’s a good time to write down what it is and why it exists.

The problem

I run a lot of agent sessions. On a normal night this workstation has four or five projects going at once, each with a few Claude Code sessions doing different jobs: one reviewing, one writing tests, one chasing a bug. Two things kept annoying me.

item.title: Maintaining an Open-Source Library With AI Agents: AGENTS.md and the Rule They Kept Breaking
item.description: On May 9th I merged #264, which added an AGENTS.md to go-proxmox and a stub CLAUDE.md that just points at it. Over the next six weeks, through the v0.8.0 migration guide on June 15th, main took 77 commits, +31,794 / -1,144 lines, went from 84 to 186 .go files, and endpoint coverage went from 30% to 100% of the Proxmox API. Most of that code was typed by coding agents, a lot of it by several at once. This is what that looked like from the maintainer’s chair, mostly the parts that went wrong, because that’s where AGENTS.md got its content.
